title: Theme Engine: unify token mapping and component overrides for dark mode and brand themes
creator: Sana Patel
description: Goal: Create a single, well-documented token mapping and a lightweight component override layer so the Redwood Console can support first-class dark mode, multiple branded themes, and runtime theme switching without component drift. This ticket covers: mapping legacy tokens to the new token namespace, defining high-level semantic tokens (surface/interactive/text/border/overlay), creating component override recipes for buttons, tables, and charts, documenting accessibility contrast targets, and delivering a test plan for rollout. Constraints: must be compatible with existing runtime theme switch API (ENG-3742), should not increase initial CSS payload by more than 6%, and must keep per-route theming fallback behavior intact.
acceptance_criteria: A canonical token map document exists mapping legacy tokens to new semantic tokens with examples for light and dark modes
Button, Table, and Chart components accept theme overrides via the existing theme API and render identically to design specs in both light and dark themes
Color contrast for body text, controls, and interactive elements meets WCAG 2.1 AA in both light and dark themes
A migration guide for devs (2 pages) plus a token export script for engineering are checked into docs and referenced in PRs
Automated snapshot tests and visual diffs added to CI for the primary console routes under light/dark/brand themes
design_notes: We move from surface-specific tokens (e.g., gray-50/gray-100) to semantic tokens: background.surface, background.elevated, text.primary, text.secondary, border.standard, interactive.primary, interactive.hover, chart.palette.{n}. Create an alias layer so components can opt into either semantic or legacy token sets during migration. For charts, provide a palette token set and an algorithmic color transform for dark mode to preserve perceptual ordering. Buttons will get explicit variants: primary/secondary/ghost/destructive with semantic token references. Tables should expose row/elevated/focus tokens and a zebra token that adapts to dark mode by shifting hue rather than brightness. Maintain iconography color tokens (icon.primary/icon.muted) instead of hard-coded fills. Figma file has component variants flagged with token references (see links).
implementation_plan: Create token mapping spreadsheet and fill initial mappings for all console tokens
Draft semantic token spec and review with ENG and PM
Add token alias export to design-tokens repo (json + CSS vars) and version as v2.0
Update Button, Table, Chart components in the component-lib to consume semantic tokens via the theming API
Add visual regression tests and run full console snapshot suite across themes
Roll out canary to 10% of traffic and monitor cost/latency and visual diffs for 72h
Publish migration guide and coordinate with platform teams for dependent services
review_feedback: PM: prefer smaller initial scope — focus on buttons/tables/charts first, defer ancillary components
ENG: require token export in both CSS variable and compact JSON formats; watch runtime parsing cost
Accessibility: increase contrast target for disabled controls in dark mode; update tokens accordingly
Design: provide color-blind-safe chart palettes as opt-in tokens
